In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the oxygen isotope values of ophicalcite carbonates are not reliable for reconstructing the original temperature of the ophicalcite formation.
the carbon and oxygen isotope values recorded in ophicalcite and pelagic sedimets are not related to the Jurassic hydrothermal processes but to later Alpine fluid-rock interaction during the orogeny.
ophicalcitic breccias are not suitable to trace the oxygen-isotope composition of ancient seawater.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the formation of ophiolite-related breccias is a process that is not unique to the Alpine orogen, but that the oxygen-isotope signature of these ophicarbonatic breccias is unique and can be used as a fingerprint for the formation of ophilolites in general.
the oxygen-isotope system of ophicalcite is not suitable to reconstruct the hydrothermal activity at the sea floor.
the oxygen-isotope composition of ophicalcite is an ever-lasting controversy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

oxygen isotope values of ophicalcite breccias are not reliable indicators of the hydrothermal conditions during their formation, and thus cannot be used to infer the temperature of hydrothermal circulation.
the interpretation of the oxygen isotopes in ophiolites is a very difficult task and should be undertaken with caution.
the oxygen isotope composition of ophicarbonatites is not a reliable indicator for hydrothermal alteration in ancient ocean–continent transitions.
